_note: Stock substances for Lab 1 (identify unknown white solids). Every numeric property has a source and a verified flag. verified:false means 'entered from memory of standard references, not yet checked by Mr. D against the cited source'. The ship gate (npm run gate) fails while any value is unverified. Solubility is g per 100 mL of solvent at 20 C, treated as independent of volume change (a simplification). Densities are true (crystal) densities, not bulk powder densities.

species.name: sodium chloride (table salt)
species.heating: no change at hot-plate temperatures; it melts at 801 C
species.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics (physical constants of inorganic compounds)

species.name: sucrose (table sugar)
species.heating: melts and caramelizes to brown near 186 C, then darkens and smokes
species.source: CRC Handbook; sucrose solubility ~204 g/100 g water at 20 C

species.name: sodium bicarbonate (baking soda)
species.heating: decomposes above about 80 C, slowly giving off CO2 and water; leaves sodium carbonate
species.source: CRC Handbook; solubility ~9.6 g/100 g water at 20 C

species.name: calcium carbonate (powdered chalk)
species.heating: no change at hot-plate temperatures; it decomposes near 825 C
species.source: CRC Handbook (calcite); solubility ~0.0013 g/100 mL at 25 C

species.name: cornstarch
species.appearance: fine white powder that squeaks when pressed
species.heating: browns and chars well above 200 C, smoking
species._formulaNote: Formula is one glucose unit of the polymer (C6H10O5)n; molar mass is per unit.
species.source: approximate true density of native starch granules ~1.5 g/cm3

species.name: citric acid (anhydrous)
species.heating: melts near 153 C to a clear liquid
species.source: CRC Handbook; solubility ~59 g/100 g water at 20 C

species.name: vinegar (5% acetic acid)
species.source: labelled 5% w/v acetic acid; density ~1.005 g/mL

species.name: iodine test solution (dilute I2 in KI)
species._note: Approximate teaching-lab strength (~0.01 M). The KI that keeps I2 dissolved is not modeled as a separate component.
